Before you start building, yes — this is broadly the scope we've worked through, and I'm glad it's all captured. Two everyday things jump out at me as missing, though, and they're basic enough to managing bookmarks that I'd want them in from the start rather than discovered later:

First, getting rid of one I no longer want. We've covered marking things read and saving copies, but I don't see anywhere I can just delete a bookmark for good — say I saved something by mistake, or it's gone stale and I never want to see it again. That's different from "read" or "set aside," and I'd expect a clear, deliberate way to remove it entirely.

Second, going back to fix one I already saved. I can tidy the title and tags at the moment I save, and I saw I can adjust an existing one when I re-paste its address — but what about a bookmark that's been sitting in my library for weeks and I just want to rename it, re-tag it, or fix a typo in my note? I'd want to open any saved bookmark and edit it directly, without having to re-paste the link to get at it.

If those two — deleting a bookmark, and editing an already-saved one anytime — are included alongside everything else, then go ahead and start building. Can you confirm they're in?
